newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Thousands march in Sofia against ruling Socialists.
newsitem.headline: Thousands march in Sofia against ruling Socialists.

text.p: Thousands of anti-government demonstrators marched in Sofia on Thursday, the fourth day of a nationwide chain of protests organised by the opposition to demand early parliamentary elections in Bulgaria.
Despite snow and sub-zero temperatures, protesters massed to chant "Resign" and "We want elections".
Thousands more marched in 11 other big cities to protest against shrinking wages eroded by the collapsing national currency.

"Those who ruled this country for five decades and brought nothing but suffering cannot lead the country out of the crisis. They must go," a leader of the opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) told the rally.
UDF deputy Alexander Bozhkov burned a copy of the draft 1997 budget, hastily approved and introduced to parliament on Saturday by the outgoing Socialist cabinet of Zhan Videnov.
"This budget is unrealistic and is reminiscent of a communist-type economy," said Bozhkov.

On Wednesday the Socialists nominated powerful Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev to become prime minister in place of Videnov, who offered his resignation on December 21 after severe criticism of his management of the economy.

The opposition says the Bulgarian Socialist Party, formed by leading Communists after the collapse of one-party rule in 1989, has failed to tackle the country's economic crisis and no longer has enough support to form a government.
The UDF has scheduled more rallies for Friday, emulating demonstrations against the Socialist government in neighbouring Yugoslavia.
Dobrev's government will be Bulgaria's ninth since the end of one-party rule in 1989.
